articles.title: Premier League Darts: Stephen Bunting fortunate, bitter pill to swallow for Danny Noppert says Wayne Mardle
articles.summary: Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle gives his views on the 2026 Premier League Darts picks; you can watch Premier League Darts live on Sky Sports from February 5 every Thursday all the way through until the finale at The O2 in London on May 28
articles.body:
The decision to pick Bunting, alongside the other wild cards of Jonny Clayton, Gerwyn Price and Josh Rock, has caused debate since Monday's announcement.

Bunting finished bottom of last year's Premier League and failed to win more than one match at any of the majors following July's World Matchplay.

He did win two World Series events and two European Tour events but Mardle thinks other played who have not been chosen for the Premier League had better seasons.

"I think that's a fortunate pick for Stephen. We know he was world No 4 going into the Worlds, now he's out of it. It would have been a tough pill for him to swallow if he was left out," he told Sky Sports .

"But, again, I think he will be the one that will breathe a sigh of relief because he didn't play poorly last year, it just took him eight weeks to get a win.

"Over the short format, you'd have thought that no-one would lose eight games on the bounce. He did, and he didn't get out of last position. He ended up rallying, to be fair, he rallied and still finished bottom."

World No 10 Noppert was the most notable admission after he made four major semi-final appearances while Nathan Aspinall also missed out. Mardle thinks "it is a bitter pill to swallow for Noppert" after an "amazing" year on the oche.

"He's had a better year than some of the players in it. But, when you know what you're getting from Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton, you know what you're getting in a Premier League, you don't know what you're getting from Danny Noppert," he said.

"You know you're going to get someone who's ultra-consistent, but is he someone that engages with the crowd? Could he become that person? Could he be someone that people switch their TV on to watch him?

"I've got a lot of time for Danny, I think he's an amazing player, and the way he played in the World Championship, it's hard to lose early in the World Championship, to come out with more credit than he went in with. He did that because that game with Justin Hood was utterly ridiculous. What's he got to do to get in?"

Mardle: Rock will relish in the Premier League

Northern Ireland's Josh Rock will be one of two debutants alongside World Championship runner-up when the Premier League begins on February 5 in Newcastle.

Rock won the World Cup of Darts with Daryl Gurney and made the semi-finals of the UK Open and World Matchplay which helped him rise into the top 10 of the PDC rankings for the first time.

Mardle said: "He's on the up and he's consistently playing well. We've seen him in the past that debutants have done alright.

"Josh is one of those players that will relish it. He's a fiery character and he seems to thrives on the competition. The Premier League is all that - it's the big stage, it's competition, it's relentless.

"Where I think he's new to the Premier League, he won't be jaded. There are some, and Gary Anderson being one of them, and Michael van Gerwen's mentioned it a lot as well, about how tough the Premier League can be when you've played it so often. It's like, 'I want a break, I don't want to be in it'. Gary says that a lot.

"But Josh has got this newness still to him. I don't see it being an issue one bit. I think he'll do really well."

Who will win this year's Premier League Darts? Luke Humphries will be defending his title and you can watch the action every single Thursday from February 5 until May 28, live on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more top sport with NOW .

articles.title: Mississippi Governor Tate Reeves hits Lane Kiffin, LSU with $195 million troll job
articles.summary: Mississippi Governor Tate Reeves is also giving Lane Kiffin a hard time after his loss to Ole Miss on Saturday. Kiffin now coaches at LSU who lost 32-24 to O...
articles.body:
Mississippi Governor Tate Reeves is also giving Lane Kiffin a hard time after his loss to Ole Miss on Saturday.

Kiffin now coaches at LSU who lost 32-24 to Ole Miss, his former university where he spent six seasons as the head football coach. He left in 2025. Several celebrities and fans have spoken out about the loss given the history, which now includes Reeves, who poked fun at the defeat.

"What does a $54 million buyout for the old coach, a $91 million contract for the new coach, and a $50 million roster get you?" Reeves asked on X. "An a-s whipping in Oxford, Mississippi!"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Reeves was referring to the buyout paid to former head coach Brian Kelly after he was fired. Kelly was dismissed from LSU in 2025 and currently works as a broadcast analyst for CBS Sports and SiriusXM. The $91 million is in reference to the 7-year contract given to Lane Kiffin to take over as the new head coach at LSU. Lastly, the $50 million refers to the estimated roster and NIL investment build-up for LSU's football team.

Despite the trolling of Reeves, many came to the defense of Kiffin in the comment section.

"We know this is y'all's Super Bowl. We chase championships in Baton Rouge. Ole miss is just another game," one fan wrote.

Another fan believes that Reeves should pay some respect to Kiffin, "You owe everything to Lane Kiffin! He built that program, recruited every player that got you that win tonight, and made ole miss relevant for the first time since the '60s. Puff your chest now because the reckoning without him is coming. Bless you!"

"A– whopping?" a fan asked before providing more context to Ole Miss' 32-24 win. "It was a good win, facilitated by an amazing player – who Kiffin brought in. Came down to the last two drives. I suppose enjoy it now. But some perspective would be good too. Success can be fleeting. Ole Miss still has the best jerseys in the world. So good."

Kiffin is staying positive and is ready for the future, noting there is "a lot of football left."

"We're 0-1 in SEC play. Again, whether win or loss, I was already ready for that, knowing, man, it feels like we've already played a season with so much emotion in the games—the first and third games and all the stuff," he told reporters at the end of the game. "Now we're right back to where we've always been and have eight SEC games to play. There's a lot of football left. We go back home next week and get a win."

Next up for LSU will be a matchup against the Texas A&M Aggies, and Ole Miss will be facing the Florida Gators on Saturday, Sept. 26.

articles.title: Mayville State QB in medically induced coma after sustaining severe head injury
articles.summary: Matt Donovan was injured on a helmet-to-helmet hit in the third quarter.
articles.body:
Mayville State announced Sunday that quarterback Matt Donovan was in a medically induced coma after suffering a head injury during the team's game against Simpson University on Saturday.

Donovan was injured in the third quarter of the NAIA team's 42-41 win on a helmet-to-helmet hit. He was life-flighted to Fargo (N.D.), which is approximately 60 miles to the southeast.

"Once he arrived in Fargo, he underwent surgery on his brain that lasted just over two hours, where they removed portions of his skull in order to release the pressure from his brain," a school statement said. "For context, the pressure in the average person's brain is a 4, his was many times more than that. After leaving surgery, he was released into the intensive care unit and is under some of the best medical care in the midwest. [Sunday morning], his eyes reacted to light in a normal manner, which caused the neurosurgeon to say last night was a win. He is still in a medically-induced coma and is fighting like crazy. Your prayers are working and encouraged at this time."

A GoFundMe started by Donovan's sister Ashley Klar had already reached nearly $30,000 as of Sunday afternoon.

"The funds raised will help support Matthew's family with lodging and dining while we are away from home, along with medical expenses related to his care and recovery," Klar wrote.

Donovan transferred to Mayville State from Minot State and previously played at Bemidji State. He played high school football at Kasson-Mantorville in Minnesota.

articles.title: Broncos vs. Jaguars third quarter recap
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars got the ball first to start the second half after closing out the first half with a last second field goal to extend their lead over...
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars got the ball first to start the second half after closing out the first half with a last second field goal to extend their lead over the Denver Broncos . Perhaps Sean Payton should have deferred like most teams do these days when they win the coin toss.

A pitch to Bhayshul Tuten immediately gained 16 yards for the Jaguars to start their next drive and then fired a bullet to Parker Washington for another first down. That put Washington at 7 catches for 98 yards in the game. From the Broncos 35-yard line, Tuten would rip off another 11 yards. That would be three straight plays of 10+ yards for the Jaguars to open up the second half.

The drive would end in a field goal after being aided by an ill-advised unnecessary roughness call on Alex Singleton . The defense was fortunate to come up with the goal line stop.

Needing a big drive, the Broncos were in danger of going three and out when Bo Nix found Jaylen Waddle open for a first down. Waddle then turned it upfield for another 10 yards. Then a double-reverse to Pat Bryant gained 15 yards into field goal range and that's where the drive would stall out.

Wil Lutz would boot it through from 45-yards out.

It felt like momentum was on the Jacksonville's side despite the trading of field goals. They had again gotten across midfield, but on a third and six the Trevor Lawrence pass to Parker Washington was short and Riley Moss came down with the interception at the Denver 35 yard line.

With the third quarter winding down, the Broncos offense had good field position and needing a touchdown to tie the game up. A big pass play by Nix to Nate Adkins got them near field goal range to close out the quarter.

articles.title: El Lugo desarbola al Zamora en media hora
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Borja Fernández termina la jornada invicto y de colíder
articles.summary: El equipo de Borja Fernández termina la jornada invicto y de colíder
articles.body: El CD Lugo se llevó tres puntos de oro del estadio zamorano y encadenó su cuarto partido consecutivo sin conocer la derrota en la cuarta jornada del Grupo 1 de Primera Federación. Los gallegos, que sentenciaron el choque antes del descanso, resistieron un asalto final del Zamora CF que solo dio frutos cuando el reloj ya marcaba el minuto 90. Ante 3.114 espectadores, el marcador terminó reflejando un 1-2 que consolida al conjunto lucense entre los aspirantes y deja al Zamora atrapado en la zona baja de la tabla. FICHA TÉCNICA Zamora: Iker Piedra, Diego Moreno (Sancho, m.46), Luismi Luengo, Gorjón, Iago Indias, Vergés (Éric, m.60), Carlos Ramos, Mauro Ramos (Hidalgo, m.60), Fabi (Pau Mascaró, m.46), Yurrieta (Carbonell, m.78), Mario Losada. CD Lugo: Embadje, Rufo, Ibaider Garriz, Pol Moreno, Pere Haro, Parrilla (Kevin Presa, m.60), Ulloa (Kike Hermoso, m.76), Arturo Palma, Gallar (Godoy, m.69), Chiqui (Berzal, m.69), Mo Dauda (Álex Costa, m.76). Goles: 0-1, m.33: Arturo Palma, 0-2, m.40: Gallar (penalti). 1-2, m.92: Carlos Ramos. Árbitro: Manuel García Gómez (Colegio extremeño). Amonestó a Luismi Luengo, Mario Losada, Yurrieta por el Zamora y a Pere Haro, Rufo, Kike Hermoso por el Lugo Incidencias: Partido disputado en el estadio Ruta de la Plata. Un primer tiempo de dos goles que marcó el destino El Lugo no necesitó demasiado para golpear donde más duele. En el minuto 33, Arturo Palma abrió la lata culminando una jugada asistida por Pere Haro, poniendo el 0-1 y silenciando las gradas locales. El delantero mexicano, el jugador de mayor valoración de mercado sobre el césped, demostró por qué es una de las referencias ofensivas del equipo dirigido desde el banquillo visitante. Apenas ocho minutos después, en el 41, llegó el golpe definitivo. El capitán Álex Gallar transformó un penalti con la sangre fría de un veterano para firmar el 0-2 y encarrilar el encuentro justo antes del intermedio. Con dos goles de renta y sin haber encajado, el Lugo se marchó a vestuarios con el partido controlado y el Zamora obligado a reinventarse. El técnico local movió ficha nada más reanudarse el juego: en el minuto 46 dieron entrada a Jaime Sancho y Pau Mascaró por Diego Moreno y Fabián Urzain, un doble cambio que evidenciaba la urgencia por revertir la situación. Poco después, en el 59, entraron también Eric Gómez y Alex Hidalgo. El Zamora quería vida, pero el muro defensivo gallego, con Pol Moreno y el argentino Rufino Lucero como bastiones en el eje, apenas concedía resquicios. El tanto tardío que llegó cuando ya no había tiempo El asedio local tuvo premio, aunque insuficiente. En el minuto 90, Carlos Ramos, el veterano centrocampista y dorsal 10 zamorano, recortó distancias para establecer el 1-2 definitivo y devolver una tenue esperanza a las gradas. Su gol, sin embargo, llegó demasiado tarde para inquietar de verdad a un Lugo que supo administrar la ventaja en los compases decisivos. El tramo final estuvo salpicado de interrupciones y tarjetas. El Lugo vio amonestados a Pere Haro (67'), Rufino Lucero (75') y Kike Hermoso (78'), mientras que en el Zamora vieron cartulina Luismi Luengo (27'), Mario Losada (45') e Izan Yurrieta (75'). El propio Yurrieta tuvo que ser sustituido por Javier Carbonell en el minuto 79 por lesión, en una tarde marcada también por la salida forzada de Pablo Parrilla González en el bando visitante, reemplazado por Kevin Presa en el 60. Lo que dice la clasificación El resultado tiene lecturas muy distintas para ambos vestuarios. El CD Lugo llega a los 10 puntos y se coloca tercero en el Grupo 1, con un balance impecable de tres victorias y un empate en cuatro jornadas, sin derrotas y con solo dos goles encajados en todo el campeonato. Los gallegos comparten los diez puntos con el líder UD Logroñés y el segundo clasificado CP Cacereño, en un arranque de temporada que invita al optimismo en tierras lucenses. La solidez defensiva es, sin duda, su gran seña de identidad: dos goles en contra en cuatro partidos hablan de un equipo compacto y difícil de batir. El Zamora CF, en cambio, se queda con cuatro puntos y ocupa la decimocuarta posición, con un registro de una victoria, un empate y dos derrotas. El conjunto rojiblanco, que suma cinco goles a favor y seis en contra, se ve arrastrado hacia la zona incómoda de la tabla y necesitará mejorar su pegada y su concentración en las áreas si quiere alejarse de los puestos de descenso. La imagen del segundo tiempo, con un equipo volcado y con hambre de gol, es el asidero al que agarrarse, pero el daño ya estaba hecho en la primera mitad. Los protagonistas de la tarde Arturo Palma fue el faro ofensivo del Lugo. El mexicano no solo abrió el marcador, sino que ejerció de referencia constante para un equipo que supo golpear en los momentos justos. Su sociedad con el resto de la línea de ataque marcó la diferencia en un choque que se decidió por detalles. Álex Gallar, con su galones de capitán, aportó el liderazgo y la contundencia desde los once metros. Su gol de penalti fue el que rompió definitivamente el partido y demostró la madurez de un futbolista clave en el esquema visitante. En el Zamora, pese a la derrota, Carlos Ramos mantuvo la fe hasta el último suspiro. Su gol en el 90, aunque solo sirviera para maquillar el resultado, refleja el carácter de un jugador que no se rinde y que deberá tirar del carro en las próximas jornadas. Balance final El 1-2 fue justo para un Lugo que hizo los deberes cuando el partido estaba abierto y que confirma su condición de bloque serio y fiable en este arranque liguero. Los de tierras gallegas no bajan del pódium y mantienen intacta su condición de invictos. El Zamora, por su parte, deberá aprender la lección: en la Primera Federación, los errores en la primera mitad se pagan caros. La reacción tardía sirve como consuelo moral, pero la tabla no entiende de matices, y los rojiblancos necesitan sumar de tres cuanto antes para no verse comprometidos en la parte baja del Grupo 1.

articles.title: El Cacereño hace feliz al Príncipe Felipe
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Julio Cobos somete al Arenas en un encuentro en el que exhibió su pegada, suma 10 de 12 puntos posibles y se coloca primero empatado con UD Logroñés y Lugo
articles.summary: El equipo de Julio Cobos somete al Arenas en un encuentro en el que exhibió su pegada, suma 10 de 12 puntos posibles y se coloca primero empatado con UD Logroñés y Lugo
articles.body: El CP Cacereño dio un golpe sobre la mesa en la cuarta jornada del Grupo 1 de Primera Federación. Ante un Arenas Club que se hunde en la parte baja, los verdes firmaron un contundente 3-0 que les mantiene en la estela de la cabeza y confirma la solidez con la que han arrancado el curso 2026/27. Un doblete de Ignacio Tellechea y un tanto de Osama Chit certificaron una tarde redonda para el conjunto extremeño. FICHA TÉCNICA 3-CACEREÑO: Diego Nieves, Sergi López, Molina, Iván Martínez (min. 83, Víctor Rodríguez), Expósito, Gete (min. 65, Toño Calvo), Nico Conesa (min. 83, Luis Sánchez), Artola (min. 65, Monerris), Tellechea, Navarro (min. 75, Iván Fernández), Osama. 0-ARENAS: Obom, Lekuna, Zubelzu, Arratibel (min. 71, Bujan), Iker García, Ibón Badiola (Larrauri, min. 62), Gael Joel (min. 71, Borrajo) Torres (min. 81, Suso), Zabaleta, Telletxea (min. 81, Palacín), Cortés. GOLES: 1-0-Min. 61. Osama. 2-0-Min. 68:Tellechea. 3-0-Min. 92:Tellechea, de penalti. ÁRBITRO:José Antonio Palomares Gutiérrez (Comité Andaluz). Amarillas a Sergi López e Iván Martínez por los locales e Ibon Badiola, Arratibel, Gael Joel y Larrauri por los visitantes. INCIDENCIAS: Partido de la cuarta jornada de la Primera Federación disputado en el estadio Príncipe Felipe con a. Los jugadores locales con una camiseta de la asociación Alzhei. Este lunes se conmemora el Dia Mundial del Alzheimer. Un guion que se resolvió tras el descanso El marcador refleja fielmente el desarrollo del choque, pero también su paciencia. El Cacereño se marchó al vestuario con el 0-0 (así lo indica el registro del descanso), incapaz de perforar una zaga vasca que resistió durante los primeros 45 minutos. El Arenas, de hecho, fue el equipo que antes se puso nervioso: vio dos amarillas en apenas seis minutos, la de Julen Zubelzu en el 16 y la de Beñat Arratibel en el 22, señal del esfuerzo defensivo al que estaba abocado. La resistencia visitante se rompió en el minuto 62. Osama Chit, el delantero marroquí del cuadro local, abrió la lata para el 1-0 y desatascó un partido que pedía a gritos un primer gol. A partir de ahí, el Cacereño soltó el freno de mano. Siete minutos después, en el 69, Ignacio Tellechea firmó el 2-0 para encarrilar definitivamente el encuentro. El propio Tellechea cerró la cuenta en el 90, esta vez desde el punto de penalti, para establecer el 3-0 definitivo y llevarse el balón a casa con su doblete. Entre medias, el técnico local movió el banquillo con criterio: en el 67 dieron entrada Toño Calvo y Alejandro Monerris por Álvaro Gete y Juan Artola, y más tarde Iván Fernández Tamayo, Runy y Víctor Rodríguez refrescaron un once que ya dominaba con comodidad. El Arenas, por su parte, agotó sus cambios buscando reacción —Jon Larrauri, Unai Buján, Ekaitz Redondo, Jesús María Sánchez Téllez y Erlantz Palacín entraron desde el banquillo—, pero no encontró el camino hacia la portería de Diego Nieves, que mantuvo su meta a cero. Las claves tácticas El Cacereño planteó el partido con un 4-5-1 diseñado para el control, con Juan Artola como referencia ofensiva inicial y un centro del campo poblado en el que Tellechea acabó siendo determinante desde su posición de mediocampista. La superioridad se tradujo en tres goles en la segunda parte, un tramo en el que el equipo de Iván Martínez —capitán sobre el césped— empujó con constancia hasta doblegar a su rival. El Arenas se ordenó en un 4-3-3 con José Luis Cortés en punta, pero el guion se le complicó pronto por la acumulación de tarjetas y la falta de mordiente arriba. La entrada de gente fresca no bastó para revertir una dinámica que, en los números, ya venía siendo preocupante para los vizcaínos. Lo que dice la clasificación El triunfo tiene lectura directa en la tabla. El CP Cacereño se sitúa segundo en el Grupo 1 con 10 puntos, fruto de tres victorias y un empate en cuatro jornadas, sin conocer la derrota. Comparte esa cifra de puntos con el líder, la UD Logroñés (también 10, con idéntica diferencia de +5 pero mayor cifra goleadora), y con el CD Lugo, tercero con 10. Los verdes presentan además el mejor balance defensivo del trío de cabeza: solo un gol encajado en todo el campeonato, un dato que este domingo se mantuvo intacto gracias a la portería a cero. Con seis goles a favor y uno en contra, el Cacereño exhibe la solidez de un aspirante serio a pelear por los puestos de privilegio. El pulso por el liderato del grupo promete ser cerrado, con tres equipos igualados a puntos y una defensa cacereña que, de momento, marca la diferencia. El Arenas, en zona de emergencia Al otro lado, el panorama es sombrío. El Arenas Club es decimonoveno con un único punto, cosechado en un empate, y suma ya tres derrotas. Su casillero goleador es demoledoramente negativo: 3 tantos a favor por 10 en contra, la peor diferencia del grupo entre los equipos con vida (-7), solo por delante de la Unión Deportiva Ourense, que cierra la tabla sin puntuar. El equipo vizcaíno ocupa plaza de descenso y necesita reaccionar con urgencia. La imagen defensiva vuelve a ser el gran problema: diez goles encajados en cuatro partidos dibujan una tendencia que exige respuesta inmediata si no quiere descolgarse del pelotón en las primeras semanas de competición. Jugadores a seguir Ignacio Tellechea fue, sin discusión, el nombre propio de la tarde. Su doblete —uno en jugada y otro de penalti— rompió el equilibrio y disparó al Cacereño hacia la victoria. El mediocampista se erige en un recurso ofensivo valioso desde la segunda línea. Osama Chit, autor del gol que abrió el marcador, aportó la referencia física en ataque que el equipo necesitaba para desatascar un partido trabado. Su tanto en el 62 fue la llave que lo cambió todo. En el Arenas, José Luis Cortés cargó con la responsabilidad ofensiva desde la punta, pero apenas recibió munición. El delantero necesitará más apoyo si el equipo quiere empezar a sumar de tres. Conclusión El 3-0 no admite discusión: el CP Cacereño fue muy superior en la segunda mitad y se aferra a la zona noble del Grupo 1 con una defensa que, por ahora, es la más fiable de la cabeza. El Arenas, en cambio, se marcha de Cáceres con las mismas dudas con las que llegó, instalado en el descenso y obligado a reaccionar. Dos trayectorias opuestas que la cuarta jornada ha dejado nítidamente dibujadas.

articles.title: Pedro Benito aprovechó un error local para dar el triunfo a la Cultural
articles.standfirst: El gaditano fue 'el más listo de la clase' y aprovechó un error gigante en la salida de balón para darle el triunfo en el 97' al conjunto leonés
articles.summary: El gaditano fue 'el más listo de la clase' y aprovechó un error gigante en la salida de balón para darle el triunfo en el 97' al conjunto leonés
articles.body: Un gol en el minuto 90 rompe un partido de tanteo y deja a la Cultural Leonesa entre los diez mejores del Grupo 1. El fútbol de la Primera Federación volvió a demostrar por qué se le considera una de las categorías más igualadas y crueles del panorama nacional. En la cuarta jornada del Grupo 1, la Cultural Leonesa se marchó de Almendralejo con los tres puntos gracias a un tanto de Pedro Benito en el minuto 90, en un desenlace que dejó al CD Extremadura sin premio pese a haber competido durante buena parte del encuentro. El marcador final, un ajustadísimo 0-1, resume la naturaleza del choque: escaso en goles, tenso en el tramo decisivo y sentenciado en el instante en que menos margen quedaba para reaccionar. FICHA TÉCNICA EXTREMADURA: Alfonso Liceras; Bekhoucha (Carlos Cordero, m.87), Rober Correa, Sergi Molina, Yael Ballesteros (Lecic, M.61), Rodrigo Escudero (Iker Burgos, m.87), Kike Márquez, Marco Manchón, Chus Villar (Nordin, m.61), Álex Macías y Diego (Espejo, m.87) CULTURAL LEONESA: Parera; Iago López, Jaime Vázquez, Jaso, Pomares (Oier López, m.87); Algobia, Bicho, Pedro Benito, Álex Cordero (Jon García, m.71), Queipo y Delgado (Escobar, m.71). GOLES: 0-1 Pedro Benito, min.96. ÁRBITRO: José María Aranda (andaluz). Amonestó con amarilla al visitante Jaime. Expulsó con roja directa al local Marco Manchón en el minuto 85. INCIDENCIAS: 4.700 espectadores en el Francisco de la Hera. Un duelo estrangulado hasta el desenlace Durante los primeros compases el partido se mantuvo cerrado, con ambos conjuntos midiéndose sin exponerse. La única amonestación de la primera mitad recayó sobre el defensa visitante Jaime Vázquez en el minuto 37, un aviso de la intensidad que empezaba a acumularse. Al descanso, el electrónico reflejaba el 0-0 con el que se llegó al intermedio. La segunda parte alteró los planes del equipo local antes de tiempo. En el minuto 63, el técnico del Extremadura se vio obligado a mover el banquillo por partida doble: Luka Lečić entró por Yael Ballesteros, sustitución marcada por una lesión, mientras Nordin Al Lal reemplazaba a Chus Villar en un cambio de corte táctico. Enfrente, la Cultural respondió en el 72 con la doble maniobra de Jon García por Álex Cardero y Antón Escobar por Jorge Delgado, buscando frescura en las posiciones de ataque. El guion dio un vuelco definitivo en el minuto 86. Marco, delantero del Extremadura, vio la tarjeta roja y dejó a los locales con diez hombres para afrontar el tramo final. Con superioridad numérica, la Cultural apretó y encontró recompensa: en el minuto 90, Pedro Benito firmó el único gol del partido para desatar la celebración visitante. El propio Benito recibiría acto seguido una amonestación, en el mismo minuto en que Róber también era amonestado por el bando local, síntoma del nerviosismo que envolvió el final. Las claves del once El Extremadura, dirigido desde el 4-3-3, apostó por un bloque con Alfonso Liceras bajo palos y una zaga formada por Ismael Bekhoucha, Róber, Sergi Molina y Alex Macías. Kike Márquez, veterano y con galones en el centro del campo, quedó señalado con una amarilla en el minuto 74, en pleno tira y afloja por el control del balón. La expulsión de Marco condicionó por completo la recta final de un equipo que se había mantenido con vida en el marcador. La Cultural Leonesa, ordenada en un 4-2-3-1, tuvo en su capitán Bicho al director de juego y en Ángel Algobia, el jugador de mayor valor de mercado del once titular visitante, a un referente en la medular. Pedro Benito, situado en la mediapunta, terminó siendo el hombre decisivo con su gol en el descuento del tiempo reglamentario. La defensa liderada por Carlos Pomares y Jaime Vázquez, junto al portero Miquel Parera, sostuvo la portería a cero que da un valor doble a la victoria. Lo que dice la clasificación El resultado tiene lecturas opuestas para cada bando. La Cultural Leonesa alcanza los 7 puntos y se instala en la décima posición del Grupo 1, con un balance de 2 victorias, 1 empate y 1 derrota. Su fortaleza queda retratada en los números: solo 2 goles a favor pero apenas 1 en contra en cuatro jornadas, la muestra de un equipo que fía su temporada a la solidez defensiva más que al espectáculo ofensivo. El triunfo en Almendralejo confirma esa identidad. Para el CD Extremadura, en cambio, la derrota agrava una situación incómoda. El conjunto azulgrana se queda con 3 puntos, fruto de 1 victoria y 3 derrotas, y ocupa la decimoséptima plaza, ya en la zona baja de la tabla. Con 2 tantos a favor y 4 en contra, el equipo paga cara su falta de pegada: en cuatro partidos apenas ha logrado perforar la meta rival en dos ocasiones. La imagen no fue mala, pero en esta categoría los detalles y las expulsiones en momentos críticos marcan la diferencia. En lo más alto del grupo, el pulso lo mantienen UD Logroñés, CP Cacereño y CD Lugo, los tres con 10 puntos y todavía invictos, separados únicamente por la diferencia de goles. La Cultural, con su victoria, se mantiene en la pelea por acercarse a los puestos nobles, mientras el Extremadura mira ya de reojo hacia abajo, donde Arenas Club (1 punto) y Unión Deportiva Ourense (0 puntos, todavía sin sumar) marcan el fondo de la clasificación. Jugadores para seguir Pedro Benito se erige en el protagonista absoluto de la jornada. Su gol en el minuto 90 no solo decidió el partido, sino que subrayó su capacidad para aparecer en el momento justo desde la mediapunta. Es, junto a Dani Queipo —el futbolista más valioso del plantel visitante—, uno de los nombres a vigilar en el proyecto leonés. En el Extremadura, Kike Márquez sigue siendo la brújula del centro del campo, un jugador de recorrido y jerarquía que deberá tirar del carro para sacar al equipo de la zona de peligro. La otra mirada apunta a Marco, cuya expulsión resultó determinante y que tendrá que reconducir su aportación tras una tarde para el olvido. Conclusión La cuarta jornada dejó un 0-1 de guante blanco resuelto en el último aliento. La Cultural Leonesa reafirma su ADN competitivo y su portería blindada; el Extremadura, en cambio, suma una nueva decepción que lo hunde en la parte incómoda de la tabla. En una categoría donde los márgenes son mínimos, un gol en el minuto 90 puede valer una posición en la clasificación y, quizá, el tono de toda una temporada.

articles.title: Samu Vázquez hace justicia al triunfo del Hércules
articles.standfirst: Los blanquiazules se imponen con un solitario gol del lateral en un partido que merecieron ganar por más diferencia
articles.summary: Los blanquiazules se imponen con un solitario gol del lateral en un partido que merecieron ganar por más diferencia
articles.body: El Hércules CF se llevó los tres puntos ante el Juventud Torremolinos CF por 1-0 en la cuarta jornada del Grupo 2 de Primera Federación, en un partido resuelto por el defensa Samuel Vázquez, autor del único tanto nada más arrancar la segunda mitad. Una victoria trabajada que devuelve el aliento al conjunto herculano y que hunde todavía más a un visitante que sigue buscando su primera alegría del curso. FICHA TÉCNICA 1 - Hércules CF: Blazic, 'Samu' Vázquez, Rentero, 'Manu' Rico (Ben Hamed, min. 82), Álex Jiménez (Mehdi Puch, min. 65), Yago Cantero ('Miki' Bosch, min. 82), 'Antoñín' (Fran Sol, min. 82), Álex Fidalgo, Andy Escudero (Obeng, min. 73), Víctor Narro y Javi Jiménez. 0 - Juventud Torremolinos CF: Javi Cuenca, Ajegun (Óscar Buch, min. 80), Martin Krug, Dioni, Cristian, Dominique (Ángel Climent, min. 63), Kaptoum, Dorgu (Petersson, min. 71), Diaby (Iván Laka, min. 73), Jualián Bandrés y Emin (Prevendini, min. 80). Goles: 1-0, min. 51: 'Samu' Vázquez. Arbitraje: El ceheginero Juan Antonio Campos amonestó con amarillas a 'Manu' Rico por el Hércules CF y a Diaby, Dioni y Cristian por el Juventud de Torremolincos CF. Incidencias: encuentro correspondiente a la jornada 4 de Primera Federación disputado en el estadio Rico Pérez de Alicante ante 9.187 espectadores. Cómo se decidió el partido El choque llegó al descanso con un empate a cero que reflejaba la igualdad de una primera mitad tacaña en ocasiones claras. El Torremolinos, ordenado en un 4-4-2, había pasado ya por el amonestador antes del intermedio: Mamadouba Diaby vio la amarilla en el minuto 15 y el veterano Dioni en el 40, señal de que el equipo andaluz tuvo que emplearse a fondo en tareas defensivas para llegar sin daños al vestuario. El guion cambió pronto en la reanudación. En el minuto 51, Samuel Vázquez apareció para firmar el 1-0, un gol de enorme valor viniendo desde la línea defensiva y que resultó a la postre definitivo. Apenas dos minutos después, en el 53, el capitán visitante Cristian Rodríguez era amonestado, en un tramo en el que el Torremolinos empezaba a acusar la desventaja y la tensión del marcador. A partir de ahí, el partido entró en una fase de relevos. El técnico visitante movió el banquillo desde el minuto 63 con la entrada de Ángel Climent por Dominique Moubeke, y siguió refrescando el ataque con Ivan Laća y Max Alex Petersson en el 72, y Óscar Buch y Mateo Prevedini en el 80, buscando el empuje que igualara la contienda. El Hércules, dirigido desde un 4-2-3-1, respondió con su propia gestión del cronómetro. Mehdi Puch-Herrantz relevó a Alejandro Jiménez (min. 64), Isaac Obeng entró por Andy Escudero (min. 72), y en el tramo final llegaron de golpe Fran Sol por Antoñín, Adrià Bosch por Yago Cantero y Nassourou Ben Hamed por el amonestado Manu Rico (que había visto la amarilla en el 78), todos ellos en torno al minuto 81. Los cambios sirvieron para congelar el resultado y llevar el 1-0 hasta el pitido final. Las claves del duelo La lectura del encuentro es la de un partido de pequeños detalles. Con un solo gol en todo el choque, el acierto en una acción concreta marcó la diferencia entre sumar de tres o irse de vacío. Que el tanto lo firmara un defensa, Samuel Vázquez, subraya además la aportación ofensiva desde segunda línea que el Hércules encontró en un día en el que las referencias arriba no terminaban de romper el muro visitante. El Torremolinos, por su parte, pagó caro el mal inicio de la segunda parte. Encajar tan pronto tras el descanso le obligó a jugar más de 40 minutos a remolque, y aunque el banquillo aportó pólvora fresca, el conjunto malagueño no logró perforar una defensa herculana que supo cerrar espacios y administrar la renta. Lo que dice la clasificación La victoria coloca al Hércules CF con 6 puntos (2 victorias, 0 empates y 2 derrotas), instalado en la zona media del Grupo 2, en la novena posición. Es un resultado que le permite recuperar el equilibrio tras un arranque irregular y mantenerse conectado con las plazas nobles de una tabla comprimida, encabezada por el Villarreal B U23 y el Real Jaén, ambos con 10 puntos. Para el Juventud Torremolinos CF, en cambio, el panorama se complica. El equipo suma 1 punto (0 victorias, 1 empate y 3 derrotas) y se hunde en la decimoséptima plaza, en pleno descenso, con un balance de 5 goles a favor y 9 en contra. La zona baja del grupo, con Algeciras CF, CE Europa y CD Teruel igualados también en un solo punto, avisa de que el recién llegado necesita reaccionar cuanto antes para no descolgarse. Los protagonistas a seguir El nombre del día es, sin discusión, Samuel Vázquez. El defensa herculano no solo firmó el único gol del encuentro, sino que lo hizo en el momento justo, al filo de la reanudación, para orientar un partido que amenazaba con atascarse. Su capacidad para sumarse al ataque y decidir choques cerrados es un argumento valioso en una competición tan igualada. En el Torremolinos, la mirada se dirige al ataque. El experimentado Dioni, pese a la amonestación temprana, sigue siendo la referencia a la que agarrarse arriba, y los revulsivos Ivan Laća y Óscar Buch aportaron piernas frescas en un tramo final en el que el equipo lo intentó sin premio. Encontrar eficacia en el área rival será la asignatura pendiente para salir del pozo. Conclusión Un 1-0 puede parecer un resultado corto, pero para el Hércules CF vale por mucho más: tres puntos de oxígeno, portería a cero y la sensación de haber sabido competir un partido incómodo. Para el Juventud Torremolinos CF, la derrota confirma la dureza del salto de categoría y la urgencia de sumar antes de que la distancia con la salvación empiece a pesar de verdad.

articles.title: Ashley Williams: Craig Bellamy's Wales 'freshened up' by captain's return as a coach
articles.summary: The return of former captain Ashley Williams to the Wales coaching team excites boss Craig Bellamy before their Nations League fixtures.
articles.body:
Wales go into their Nations League openers aiming to shut out Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland.

With that kind of challenge, Craig Bellamy's squad might need all the defensive help they can get for games against Portugal, Denmark and Norway.

Cue Ashley Williams, the centre-back described by Bellamy as Wales' "greatest captain" of the modern era.

Williams was skipper as Wales reached the semi-finals of Euro 2016 against Ronaldo and Portugal, the peak of an international career that earned him 86 caps, wearing the armband for more than half of those appearances.

Now 42, the former Everton and Swansea City defender will not be adding to those appearances.

Instead, he will form part of a new-look Bellamy backroom team that the Football Association of Wales (FAW) hope will add a missing ingredient in the bid to reach Euro 2028.

Bellamy says Williams – and fellow new coach Alan Sheehan – will help provide "a different dynamic".

Colwill's 'surreal' Ronaldo and Haaland ambition

Wilson major Wales injury concern for Nations League

With Bellamy losing two key assistants just weeks after it seemed the Wales boss himself would walk away from the job amid interest from Burnley , Williams' arrival was something of a surprise.

His coaching experience has been limited to informal roles and fans are accustomed to seeing the much-admired ex-captain in the Match of the Day studio.

Sheehan, too, was not an expected announcement, with the former Leeds, Leicester and Luton full-back out of work since November 2025 when he was sacked by Swansea City following a relatively unsuccessful seven-month stint.

They replace James Rowberry, who has opted to focus on his role with Mark Robins at Stoke City , and Piet Cremers, a man whose analytical work Bellamy said meant "everything" but left to join Belgium's Club NXT in July.

Cremers spent time under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City and worked with Bellamy and Vincent Kompany during their successful period at Burnley.

He was often the person Bellamy turned to mid-match, but Bellamy says he was already keen to take on more of the tasks that Cremers performed.

"I loved this summer interviewing people, seeing who could add to us," said the 47-year-old, who has seen former Wales midfielder and now Tottenham assistant Andrew Crofts remain part of the setup.

"It freshens you up, gives you a different eye. Different strengths coming in means a different dynamic to how you work, which leaves me quite excited."

The obvious strength Williams brings is his personality.

Past teammates for club and country will queue up to attest to his character as a player and a person.

With Bellamy's Wales a young side, it mirrors the role the more experienced Williams played while on the field.

As senior to the likes of Gareth Bale and Aaron Ramsey, he was a leader among equals.

"I played underneath Ash as a captain, and he was a great leader in the dressing room and led by example in the way he conducted himself on and off the pitch," says Euro 2016 colleague Sam Vokes.

"He can be someone who speaks from experience and [will] go into that dressing room and immediately command respect.

"Portugal and Denmark away, he has played in those environments.

"He will be able to speak to the lads that are going out in those environments because he led by example, and led in the trenches many times."

Bellamy agrees, having retained a friendship with the former Swansea skipper after sharing a dressing room with Wales.

"In my time he's been our greatest captain," says Bellamy. "Some ex-players with a certain presence can really add something, but also his knowledge of the game is really high, his football IQ is really high."

The appointments come against the backdrop of Wales' failure to reach the World Cup and the beginnings of criticism around the side's openness.

"He'll bring some unique skills, particularly when you play Nations League A games when you have to defend a lot," said FAW chief football officer Dave Adams of Williams' appointment on the Feast of Football podcast.

"Some of the dark arts of defending, he'll bring some interesting things for the players to think about."

There is the thought that Williams would also be prepared to challenge Bellamy's thinking – seen as healthy part of a management team.

But while Bellamy says he is keen to lean on Williams' defensive know-how, it will still be the former Liverpool, Manchester City and Newcastle forward's managerial message.

"With his position, sometimes it's easier coming from a player who's been in there," said Bellamy - a former Wales captain himself.

"Now, I'll lead a lot on the information, but it's nice for me to be able to ask 'What would you see with this? If you played there, how did you feel when I asked you to do that? Is that possible? Is that not possible?' I believe he'll be a huge asset to me."

Sheehan's appointment also suggested a more defensive focus.

The former Republic of Ireland Under-21 international was seen to have a pragmatic style at Swansea.

But it appears Wales will look to benefit from the 40-year-old's eye for set-piece work, something he has also been responsible for during previous coaching roles at Luton and Southampton.

"We really want someone who is in tune with restarts and set-pieces," added Adams.

"In these sorts of games they could be the factor that give us a chance to win the game, because they are going to be very hard games to play in.

"We realise the importance of attacking and defending set-pieces in these next six games, and feel Alan and [goalkeeping coach] Martyn Margetson will bring that level of detail to help the team be best prepared for these games."

articles.title: Vincent Tan: Cardiff City owner's 1,000 days without attending a game
articles.summary: BBC Sport Wales assess Vincent Tan's often controversial stewardship of Cardiff City as his absence continues.
articles.body:
Rishi Sunak was Prime Minister, Wham had their first Christmas number one song and Vincent Tan last attended a Cardiff City game.

It was Boxing Day 2023 when the club's owner watched a 2-2 draw against Plymouth that left the Bluebirds two points from the Championship play-off places.

One thousand days have since passed without further sight of a divisive and elusive character in the Welsh capital.

When things go wrong on the pitch, such as relegation to League One in May 2025, the fans' anger is inevitably directed his way.

Tan's absence has been criticised but without his money - he took over the club in 2010 - the club would surely struggle to even exist.

On the day the Malaysian billionaire reaches the curious milestone, BBC Sport Wales examines his stewardship of the club.

Colwill's 'surreal' Ronaldo and Haaland ambition

Moylan double ends Cardiff's winless start against Charlton

Plenty has happened over the past 1,000 days since Tan last turned up to a Cardiff match.

The Bluebirds are on to their third permanent boss in that time having been relegated to the third tier before bouncing back with promotion the following year.

A planned visit last season never materialised and a slow start in the Championship this season has been compounded by injuries and an inability to bring in new players on transfer deadline day.

"It's not a good look when the owner himself doesn't turn up to see the team that he owns," said former captain Jason Perry, who played for the club for a decade between 1987 and 1997.

"It's not good knowing the owner's not here but there's no infrastructure here to carry that.

"Not only are we not seeing him, we're not hearing anything and that's the disappointment."

Keith Morgan, of the Cardiff City Supporters Trust and chair of the Fan Advisory Board, shares Perry's views.

"It's the total lack of communication rather than lack of physical presence," he said.

"He hasn't even communicated by way of a video message or an email. No messages on the club website.

"One of my criticisms is that he hasn't got the right structure in place at senior level.

"We don't have anyone with football knowledge on the board, which could have saved some excesses which cost him some money in the past."

However, head coach Brian Barry-Murphy spent four weeks in Malaysia with Tan and his family during the summer after masterminding a return to the Championship.

"His knowledge of the team and what we did last season was beyond what I expected. He doesn't miss a trick," said Barry-Murphy.

"His messages to me are always the same.

"I've not seen many people as busy as him, so I'm sure when he can, he'll be here, and when he does come, I'll be there for him."

Tan has been a divisive figure ever since becoming Cardiff owner in 2010.

He sparked controversey among supporters when rebranded the club from blue to red in 2012, including a change to the club badge, before reversing the decision two and a half years later.

However, he has also overseen and funded two promotions to the Premier League and managed the club's debt.

"Over the course of the last decade the club has lost the thick end of £200m," said football finance expert Kieran Maguire.

"That has been subsidised effectively by Vincent Tan.

"Somebody's had to put their hand in their pocket every month to make sure the lights are kept on and the wages are paid. That person has been Tan."

In June he converted £42m of the club's debt to him into equity, nearly halving the amount Cardiff owes to its majority shareholder.

That figure previously stood at almost £90m in the club's last accounts for the financial year ending 31 May 2025.

Due to changes in the cost control rules this summer, Maguire explained, clubs are increasingly turning to benefactors and owners to cover losses by investing in shares, which are not repayable, rather than loans.

"I would describe it as a bit like the bank of mum and dad," Maguire added.

"A kid can never afford to pay money back, and as a dad you'll never ask for it back, but in theory it's a loan. That's what Vincent Tan has done.

"It's commonplace, especially in the Championship because the average losses in that division are £400,000 a week. That money comes from the owners."

Reaching the 1,000-day milestone may alarm some Cardiff fans, but it is becoming more frequent in English football amid global ownership.

Earlier this month, Blackburn Rovers co-owner Balaji Rao became the first member of the Venky's ownership group to attend a game at Ewood Park since 2018.

Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour went nearly 13 years without attending a match while Everton owner Dan Friedkin has yet to go to a home game since completing a takeover of the club in December 2014 and has not spoken to David Moyes since he returned as manager.

articles.title: Arbeloa, que sigue sin ganar en la Premier, se 'Mourinhiza' y ataca a los árbitros ingleses
articles.standfirst: "Todo estuvo a su favor (del Manchester United). Todas las decisiones les beneficiaron. A los árbitros no les gusta que el Manchester United pierda"
articles.summary: "Todo estuvo a su favor (del Manchester United). Todas las decisiones les beneficiaron. A los árbitros no les gusta que el Manchester United pierda"
articles.body: Álvaro Arbeloa, amigo y alumno futbolístico de Jose Mourinho, protagonizó unas controvertidas declaraciones en Craven Cottage después de que a su Fulham se le escapase el triunfo ante el Manchester United en el último minuto. El Fulham de Arbeloa sigue sin ganar en la Premier League y sólo suma dos puntos en los cinco primeros partidos, lo que deja a los 'Cottagers' en puestos de descenso. Álvaro Arbeloa sorprendió en rueda de prensa al asegurar que a los árbitros de la Premier League "no les gusta" que el Manchester United pierda. El 'Daily Mail' publica que la airada protesta le acarreará a Arbeloa una sanción de la FA. El técnico español arremetió contra los árbitros por no señalar una falta de Harry Maguire 35 segundos antes del gol del empate del United. "Estuvimos muy, muy cerca. Tuvimos un poco de mala suerte otra vez, pero sabíamos que iba a ser difícil contra un gran equipo y hemos visto lo que ha hecho el árbitro durante el partido", comentó el ex del Real Madrid. Arbeloa se fue encendiendo dejando unas declaraciones que han llamado la atención del universo futbolístico británico: "Todo estuvo a su favor (del Manchester United); basta con ver la falta de Harry Maguire. Todas las decisiones les beneficiaron. Después del partido contra el Manchester City, supe que no les gusta que el Manchester United pierda". "Estuvimos muy, muy cerca de nuestra primera victoria, así que ahora estamos un poco disgustados. Creo que hicimos un buen partido", subrayó. Arbeloa defendió el trabajo de sus pupilos y destacó que "obviamente no fue un partido fácil para nosotros —estábamos en el último puesto—, pero mostramos personalidad con el balón y fuimos valientes. Hubo momentos en los que tuvimos que defender, pero en general hicimos un buen partido". "Ahora tenemos que conseguir la primera victoria. Si analizas nuestros primeros cinco partidos, ya nos hemos enfrentado al Manchester United y al Chelsea, y hemos jugado en Anfield y en Sunderland", recordó.

articles.title: Dominick Goodman playing long game as he builds Walnut Hills football
articles.summary: Cincinnati football legend Dominick Goodman is preaching patience in building Walnut Hills from the ground up.
articles.body:
For most of his football life, Dominick Goodman knew what winning looked like.

At Colerain, Goodman was the quarterback of a 15-0 state championship team in 2004 , earning All-American honors as the anchor of one of the most dominant seasons in Ohio high school football history.

With the University of Cincinnati Bearcats , Goodman became one of the most productive wide receivers in program history. He still ranks in UC football's top four in receptions, receiving yards and touchdown catches. Goodman's UC squads (2005-2008) went a combined 33-18, finished No. 17 in the final AP poll twice, won a pair of bowl games and reached the program's first-ever New Year's Six bowl in 2008.

Dominick Goodman | Photos of Walnut Hills coach in his playing days

After years of football where winning was the expectation, Goodman is now learning what it means to build as the head coach at Walnut Hills High School.

Through four games, Goodman's Eagles are 0-4. Those losses have come by 37, 40, 24 and 35 points. But when Goodman talks about his first season, the scoreboard is not a hot topic.

"I'm not worried about wins and losses," Goodman told The Enquirer. "I'm more worried about are we getting better each week?"

For someone as competitive as Goodman, that might sound strange. But Walnut Hills has been searching for stability for years. The Eagles haven't had a winning season since 2011, their final year in the Fort Ancient Valley Conference. Since joining the Eastern Cincinnati Conference in 2012, Walnut Hills has averaged 2.5 wins per season.

The Eagles went a combined 3-28 in three seasons before Goodman's arrival. They haven't won more than two games since 2019. Goodman is well-versed in the program's recent struggles. He also knows what it takes to change it.

He came to Walnut Hills this spring, leaving his offensive coordinator position at Talawanda after helping lead the program to a high-scoring offense that featured one of the nation's top rushers. In 2025, the Braves won a playoff game for the first time in a full season since 1991. Before that, he helped develop players at New Miami.

"It was a perfect situation to help me grow as a coach," Goodman said of the Walnut Hills job. "I've been in programs where we've had to develop and start from the bottom and work our way up to where we transition into a football school. I saw the opportunity here to do the same thing."

The first step is changing the culture in the program.

"Coming into a situation where they had losing seasons, it was a bad culture, leadership wasn't there," Goodman said. "The main focus for this year is building that culture, building that foundation and getting the kids to love and enjoy football."

That process has helped Goodman redefine what success looks like this season. Walnut Hills is a young team with a dozen underclassmen playing. There are only four seniors and juniors in the starting lineup. Some upperclassmen have only played football a few years.

"You're teaching them from the ground up," Goodman said. "That's what I love about it because I love coaching and developing kids and seeing them get better."

For Goodman, improvement won't necessarily show up on the scoreboard this fall. He sees players getting bigger, faster and stronger. Players who were overwhelmed by the speed of the game in the season-opener are beginning to slow it down mentally and make plays.

"I tell the kids every day, there's no point if we're not getting better," Goodman said. "You can see strides.

"I'm a competitor at the end of the day. I want to see results now, but you have to be patient."

Goodman's own playing career taught him the value of hard work. He said he was never the fastest or the strongest, describing himself as "always average." What made him stand out was his willingness to work.

"I worked hard, trained all the time, pushed myself so I could outwork everybody to put myself in a position to succeed," he said. "That's what all of these kids have to learn."

He's trying to teach that lesson to players in a program that has grown accustomed to losing. He's also teaching some basic fundamentals of the game.

Goodman said a misconception former players have about coaching is assuming every player has a firm grasp of the game's basics. That's not the case.

"We assume a kid, especially high school kids, know what a three-point stance is or a slant," he said. "We assume a lot of things, but when it comes down to it, we're teachers."

Goodman's first got a taste of coaching from former Colerain coach Tom Bolden, who gave him an opportunity to work alongside him while Goodman was still playing Arena Football. He retired from football and worked as a behavioral specialist at Cincinnati Children's Hospital and was the YMCA's director of sports and fitness before arriving at Talawanda, where he realized coaching was his career path.

His players are aware of his history. Their parents, many around Goodman's age, know the stories. But Goodman wants them to understand that highlights aren't the important part.

"It's all about work. Put in work; get results," he said.

Those results don't happen overnight. That's why Goodman is thinking down the road while he lays the groundwork in year 1.

"By Week 10, if we don't get a win or we get one win, it doesn't matter as long these kids get better," Goodman said. "I know what's happening in the future. I'm always thinking two, three years ahead."

Goodman also knows that's not the easiest message to sell in a program desperate for wins, but it's an essential one as Walnut Hills needs to learn how to walk before it can climb out of its perennial place in the ECC cellar.

"I don't care if you're Nick Saban; you can't turn it around just like that," Goodman said. "You gotta build, grow and develop kids."

articles.title: Chiefs Outlast Colts To Get A 33-30 Overtime Win
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs had to battle all night, but they finally got an OT win over Indianapolis.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs managed to squeak past a surprisingly feisty Indianapolis Colts team in a back-and-forth battle that went to overtime, with the Chiefs getting a 33-30 win on a 40-yard field goal from kicker Harrison Butker on the last play of the game.

It was a tight, entertaining game through out, starting with a first half full of back-and-forth scores. The Chiefs spotted the Colts a touchdown to start the game as Indy controlled the ball for over six minutes. The drive featured a nice balance of runs and short passes, with quarterback Daniel Jones finishing off the drive with a one-yard TD pass to tight end Tyler Warren .

The Chiefs came back with a field goal after a short drive, with Butker hitting from 46 yards out. The Colts then gifted them with a Daniel Jones interception that cornerback Kristian Fulton accepted, and a 13-yard touchdown pass to tight end Travis Kelce made it 10-7 Chiefs at the end of the first quarter.

Another short drive produced an Indy field goal from Spencer Schrader to tie the game and 10-10 to start the second quarter, and Indy added another one after a Butker miss to make it 13-10.

The two teams then traded touchdowns, with Kansas City scoring first on a one-yard touchdown pass to receiver Xavier Worthy to make it 17-13, but an explosive 24-yard TD run from running back Jonathan Taylor made it 20-17 at the half.

The Chiefs used an explosive play of their own to take the lead back to start the third quarter, as a 45-yard strike from Mahomes to receiver Tyquan Thornton got the ball to the one-yard line. It took a bit, but Mahomes finally hit receiver Jaden Royal in the back of the end zone to make it 24-20.

Kansas City put together another impressive drive to end the quarter, but they couldn't finish the drive and had to settle for another short Butker field goal that made it 27-20 going into the fourth.

The Colts were resilient on this particular night, however, and they came back with another impressive touchdown, with Taylor finishing it off with a five-yard run to tie the game at 27-27. Both teams had late chances after that, but the fourth quarter ended with that score and the game went to overtime.

The Chiefs took control on the opening drive of OT, starting with a 30-yard pass to Thornton, followed by a pass for a first down to Kelce. But the drive stalled in the red zone, and Butker came on to kick a field goal from 31 yards out and make it 33-30.

The Colts came right back with a field goal of thier own, with the big play being a 48-yard pass to Laquon Treadwell that almost became a fumble recovery for Kansas City. It put the Colts in the red zone, but they couldn't finish their drive, and Schrader came on to kick a 38-yard field goal that tied things back up at 30-30.

The Chiefs then closed it out with a final clock-killing drive, with the key play being a third-and-1 near midfield. Instead of running, Mahomes threw a short floater to Walker that went for 22 yards and set up the winning 40-yard field goal from Butker.

articles.title: Final score: Chiefs defeat Colts 33-30 on 'Sunday Night Football'
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 on 'Sunday Night Football' in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs saw their regular-season record advance to 2-0 after they earned a thrilling 33-30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on 'Sunday Night Football' in Week 2.

Star running back Kenneth Walker III led the way for Kansas City 's offense with 117 rushing yards on 24 attempts and 61 receiving yards on four receptions — the last of which helped seal the victory for the Chiefs in overtime.

Patrick Mahomes put up elite numbers in Week 2, completing 32 of his 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. The two-time MVP was also Kansas City's second-leading rusher behind Walker with 17 yards gained on two carries.

Legendary tight end Travis Kelce , speedy wide receiver Xavier Worthy , and promising wideout Jalen Royals each caught touchdown passes from Mahomes.

Defensively, the Chiefs relied on standout performances from their linebacking corps against Indianapolis' impressive ground attack. Star backers Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill tallied 13 and eight combined tackles, respectively. Veteran defensive back Kristian Fulton came down with a game-changing interception in the first quarter and logged two combined tackles.

With back-to-back wins over equine-branded franchises under their belts, the Chiefs will look ahead to their Week 3 matchup against the 0-2 Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27.

articles.title: Aarón Mayol convierte sus sueños en realidad: "No puedo describir lo que sentí cuando marqué el gol"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista de 2008 se muestra con un golazo en Mestalla, aunque no sirvió para que el Valencia sumara ningún punto
articles.summary: El centrocampista de 2008 se muestra con un golazo en Mestalla, aunque no sirvió para que el Valencia sumara ningún punto
articles.body: “Estoy muy contento por el gol. Pero es una pena no haber podido llevarnos los tres puntos, pero creo que el trabajo del equipo ha sido espectacular”. Aarón Mayol resumía el estado de ánimo del vestuario valencianista al término de una noche de emociones cruzadas en Mestalla. El centrocampista de 18 años marcó este domingo su primer gol con el primer equipo del Valencia, en su estreno oficial como titular en el estadio valencianista, pero la derrota por 2-3 ante la Real Sociedad dejó el festejo incompleto. El canterano había soñado durante años con un momento como este. Lo reconoció después del encuentro, cuando recordó que debutar en Mestalla era “un sueño” para cualquier jugador formado en la Academia. El gol llegó en el minuto 57. Tras un rechace en la frontal, Mayol armó una volea seca que superó a Álex Remiro y provocó un estallido de alivio en las gradas. Era el 1-1 y también el primer tanto del Valencia en casa en la presente Liga. "No puedo describir lo que sentí cuando marqué el gol. Fue un cúmulo de sensaciones". El Valencia atraviesa uno de los momentos más delicados de los últimos años, con cambio de entrenador, reconstrucción deportiva y una posición comprometida en la clasificación. Pero la mejor noticia volvió a llegar desde las categorías inferiores. El joven mediocentro, nacido en 2008, apenas había debutado unos días antes en Mendizorroza, donde Óscar Sánchez le dio la titularidad en la victoria ante el Alavés. Frente a la Real Sociedad confirmó que aquello no había sido una apuesta puntual. La trayectoria de Mayol explica en parte la confianza que ha generado dentro del club. Formado durante más de una década en la cantera del Levante, llegó al Valencia en 2025 y su progresión fue inmediata. Se proclamó campeón con el Juvenil A, dio el salto al Mestalla y el club decidió renovar su contrato hasta 2029 para blindar a una de las joyas de la Academia. Hace apenas unos meses seguía compitiendo en categorías formativas; ahora se ha convertido en el primer futbolista nacido en 2008 que debuta oficialmente con el Valencia en Primera división. Su irrupción no responde únicamente a una emergencia deportiva. Óscar Sánchez ya lo conocía de su etapa en el juvenil y después en el filial. En Vitoria le entregó las llaves del centro del campo, protegido por la experiencia de Guido, y el futbolista respondió completando los 90 minutos con una actuación destacada. Por eso fue directo al once que el técnico del final repitió una semana después La noche, sin embargo, quedó marcada por el resultado. La Real Sociedad se adelantó con un gol de Luka Sucic antes del descanso. Mayol devolvió la esperanza al Valencia tras la reanudación. Más tarde, Carlos Soler hizo el 1-2 de penalti, un tanto en propia puerta de Beitia estableció el 2-2 y, cuando Mestalla ya empujaba convencido de una remontada, Ander Barrenetxea firmó el definitivo 2-3 en el tiempo añadido. Aun así, el protagonista de la noche quiso quedarse con el mensaje colectivo. “Todos dentro del vestuario somos conscientes de que este es el camino”, explicó. Seguramente por ahí viene el sentido del abrazo entre Mayol, Aimar Blázquez, Otorbi y otros jugadores formados en la cantera tras el pitido final. El propio futbolista la interpretó como una muestra del trabajo que se realiza en la Academia. “La cantera está para ayudar al primer equipo”, concluye.

articles.title: El jueves comienza la era Javier Aguirre en Valencia: llegada, presentación... y reconstrucción
articles.standfirst: El entrenador mexicano será el próximo inquilino del banquillo valencianista
articles.summary: El entrenador mexicano será el próximo inquilino del banquillo valencianista
articles.body: Javier Aguirre llega el jueves a Valencia. Así está previsto al menos.Será el día en el que empiece su era en Mestalla, en principio hasta junio próximo, pero con opción de ser alargada una temporada más, si se cumplen algunos requisitos, como ya hemos informado en MARCA. La llegada del 'Vasco' a Valencia será seguida por la oficialidad de su fichaje (quizá esto se produzca antes incluso); la presentación del entrenador mexicano; y el comienzo de su trabajo junto a sus dos principales ayudantes: el catalán Pol Lorente, preparador físico y hombre de absoluta confianza de Javi, y el mallorquín Toni Amor. Ambos le han acompañado en su carrera en los últimos equipos de Aguirre, incluida la Selección mexicana. Javier reside actualmente en México, aunque mantiene siempre su casa de Madrid. Será tras su llegada cuando comience a poner las bases del nuevo proyecto valencianista que tiene básicamente un objetivo: mantener la categoría pues el equipo es penúltimo en la tabla, sólo un punto por encima del Málaga, colista con tres puntos. El debut oficial del 'Vasco' en el banquillo será dentro de tres fines semana en Santander ante el Racing, un rival,en teoría, por la permanencia. Javier tendrá dos semanas largas para preparar el choque y entrenar con sus nuevos pupilos.

articles.title: Indiana Football: A Deeper Look At The Offense In Win Over Western Kentucky
articles.summary: Using some analytics and taking a closer look at the entire game, here are some things that stood out in Indiana's win over Western Kentucky.
articles.body:
When you look at the final score in Indiana's win over Western Kentucky , it's obviously pretty impressive. Beating a team 38-0 is as close to a perfect outcome as a team can achieve. However, nothing is ever perfect in football, so it's always fun to take a deeper look at how the game played out. Indiana is 3-0, and has dominated through three weeks, and the film is showing that.

Using a tool like Pro Football Focus allows us to see what happened on a player-by-player basis and gives some insight as to how the game really went. It's not gospel, but there are some things that just don't show up in the box score that can tell another part of the story.

Once again, Becker was virtually unguardable and found the end zone. Each week, he's racking up a lot of yards and scoring a lot of touchdowns. He did only find the end zone once this week, but it was from 79 yards out. When the clock ran out, he had caught five passes for 127 yards and that long touchdown. It's not a surprise that he graded out best on pass plays with a day like that. He wasn't awesome as a run blocker, but he was good enough for the No. 1 spot this week.

It's also not a surprise that Hoover is near the top of this list. He's been incredibly efficient every single week. Against WKU, he was 18-of-24 for 273 yards and two touchdowns. He didn't throw quite as many touchdowns this week, but he was still on fire. Life after Fernando Mendoza has been pretty good after all.

As good as Becker was, Marsh was right there with his running mate. In fact, you could make an argument that Marsh was Hoover's favorite target against WKU. The sophomore reeled in seven receptions for 81 yards. He didn't score, but he was reliable for Hoover all day long. He was also better than Becker was as a run blocker on the day, which helped both Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard rush for 199 yards and three touchdowns combined.

Marsh actually paced the wide receiver group with 47 snaps played. Becker was second with 44, while Shazz Preston was third with 37 snaps, 11 more than Tyler Morris , who had been a pretty big part of the offense through two weeks.

articles.title: Brian Brobbey joins elite Premier League list after Man City hat-trick
articles.summary: Brian Brobbey produced a performance to remember at Manchester City on Sunday, even though Sunderland left the Etihad empty-handed after an extraordinary 5-3...
articles.body:
Brian Brobbey produced a performance to remember at Manchester City on Sunday, even though Sunderland left the Etihad empty-handed after an extraordinary 5-3 defeat.

The Dutch striker's hat-trick made him only the fourth player in Premier League history to score three times against a team that began the day top of the table, according to Opta.

Brobbey follows an exclusive group consisting of Robbie Fowler, Dirk Kuyt and Romelu Lukaku .

Fowler was the first to achieve the feat when he scored a hat-trick for Liverpool against Aston Villa in November 1998. Kuyt then produced three goals for Liverpool against Manchester United in March 2011, before Lukaku matched the achievement for West Brom against United in May 2013.

Brobbey's treble came in a match that Sunderland repeatedly refused to let Manchester City run away with. The 24-year-old scored three times as the visitors twice fought back from behind, with his third goal bringing Sunderland within one of City at 4-3.

However, Erling Haaland eventually settled the contest with a late goal, preserving City's perfect start to the Premier League season.

The hat-trick also ended Brobbey's wait for his first goal of the campaign in emphatic fashion.

He became the first Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick since Jermain Defoe against Swansea City in January 2016 and only the fifth player to score a top-flight treble for the club.

There was another unusual distinction attached to Brobbey's performance: he became only the sixth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick in a match his team ultimately lost. The previous instance came when Blackburn Rovers' Roque Santa Cruz scored three against Wigan Athletic in December 2007.

Brobbey admitted afterwards that the result made his achievement difficult to enjoy.

"It's hard being on the losing side when you're scoring three goals," he told Sky Sports.

Despite the defeat, the striker heads into the international break having finally opened his league account in spectacular fashion — and with his name now alongside some of the Premier League's most memorable hat-trick feats.

articles.title: Haaland completes Premier League scoring set with Sunderland goal
articles.summary: Erling Haaland has scored against every team he has faced in the Premier League after finding the net against Sunderland in Manchester City’s 5-3 victory at...
articles.body:
Erling Haaland has scored against every team he has faced in the Premier League after finding the net against Sunderland in Manchester City 's 5-3 victory at the Etihad Stadium.

The Norwegian completed the set in the 81st minute, scoring for the first time against Sunderland at the third attempt. He has now found the net against all 25 Premier League opponents he has played against since arriving in England.

Haaland has been particularly prolific against West Ham , scoring 11 goals in eight league appearances. Crystal Palace and Wolves have conceded 10 each, while Manchester United have seen him score nine times in eight league meetings.

His record against Arsenal stands at six goals in eight appearances, while Fulham , Everton and Brighton have also regularly featured among his goalscoring victims.

Interestingly, Haaland has scored against Sheffield United, Luton Town and Coventry City despite facing each club only once in the Premier League.

The Sunderland goal also took Haaland to five Premier League goals this season, giving him an early lead in the Golden Boot race. He has already won the award in three of his four Premier League campaigns with City, including his record 36-goal haul in 2022/23.

Overall, Haaland now has 117 Premier League goals in 137 appearances, placing him among the competition's highest scorers since its 1992 rebrand.

His start to the 2026/27 campaign has been equally prolific across all competitions, with seven goals in seven appearances.

Haaland's latest milestone also adds to his remarkable scoring record for City. He recently moved into third place on the club's all-time goalscoring list and now has 169 goals in 205 appearances.

Only Eric Brook, with 177 goals, and Sergio Aguero , who holds the club record with 260, remain ahead of him.

articles.summary: Paco González desvela que "Florentino Pérez se ha enfadado muchísimo de que Enrique Riquelme estuviese en el palco presidencial del Metropolitano"
articles.body: Paco González informó en el programa 'Tiempo de Juego' de la Cadena COPE sobre el "lío" protagonizado por Florentino Pérez en el palco presidencial del Estadio Riyadh Air en el derbi madrileño. "Florentino Pérez se ha enfadado muchísimo de que Enrique Riquelme estuviese en el palco presidencial del Metropolitano", desveló Paco González ("Mi relación con Florentino es cero, ahora estoy en el lado oscuro"). Posteriormente Juanma Castaño explicó en 'El Partidazo' de COPE más detalles sobre el "lío en el palco" de Florentino Pérez durante el derbi que el Atlético acabó ganando 2-1. "Florentino monta una muy gorda diciendo que a qué viene eso de que esté Riquelme (candidato a la presidencia del Madrid al que Florentino ganó las elecciones) en el palco", empieza explicando. Juanma Castaño relata que "en la comida entre directivas en el antepalco antes de que empezase el partido Florentino Pérez, que va al Metropolitano porque tiene muy buena relación con Enrique Cerezo... Y a Miguel Ángel Gil, que no va al Metropolitano, no puede ni verlo... Estando la comida alguien le dice a Florentino 'estamos enterados de que está invitado al palco presidencia Enrique Riquelme'". "Florentino Pérez monta en cólera y dice que se pira, que se va. Que como se cruce con él en algún momento que se va del palco. Le calman, Florentino se queda al partido... pero monta una muy gorda diciendo que a qué viene eso de que esté Riquelme en el palco presidencial", destaca sobre el conflicto.

articles.title: St George flag raisers could face fines under new council rules
articles.summary: Local authorities are looking at ways to crackdown on flags placed on public buildings and lamposts.
articles.body:
People who put flags on public lamp-posts and railings could face prison or fines under new rules being considered by councils.

It comes as authorities across the West of England say they have had to pay thousands of pounds to have the flags removed.

Bristol Lib Dem councillor Stephen Williams said councils are in a "cat-and-mouse situation", with workers taking the flags down and then people putting them back up again.

Beginning in the summer of 2025, thousands of St George flags have appeared in towns and cities across England, with individuals and groups behind them saying they wanted to celebrate patriotism.

Bristol City Council said it has spent about £50,000 on removing flags across the city, but explained the figure does not include the amount of time allocated to officers to conduct site visits, administration and respond to enquiries.

The city council is now considering taking a similar approach to Oxfordshire County Council in obtaining a High Court injunction which will prohibit flags on public furniture.

If approved, any person breaching the order could face prison, a fine or having their assets seized.

Williams said putting flags up on lamp-posts is dangerous.

"Unfortunately we're in a situation where our highways contractors have taken down hundreds of flags, they pretty soon go up again, so we're in a cat-and-mouse situation," Williams said.

"There is divided opinion about the meaning of people putting up flags on council lamp-posts or railings."

In Somerset, the council said the issue has cost taxpayers more than £2,900 between August 2025 and August 2026.

A spokesperson for Somerset Council said it will look at "recovering costs for removal from those responsible".

"It's important to remember that many residents do not support these unauthorised public displays," a spokesperson added.

"If we want Somerset to remain a welcoming and vibrant place then we need to ensure flags are used to foster belonging, not division."

South Gloucestershire Council has taken a robust approach and introduced a policy to remove them.

It previously told the Local Democracy Reporting Service , that unauthorised flags are a "serious matter".

Lib Dem councillor Maggie Tyrrell and Labour councillor Ian Boulton said the way some flags were being used went against the values of the South Gloucestershire community.

They said: "We recognise that national flags can bring vibrancy, pride and a sense of unity to our communities – especially during major events and periods of national celebration.

"However, their placement in unauthorised locations and recent campaigns and behaviours linked to the unauthorised display of flags have caused genuine concern among many residents."

Wiltshire Council does not plan to put in place any kind of enforcement campaign and said it is dealing with incidents on a case-by-case basis.

"Our concern isn't with the flags themselves, but with where they're displayed," David Bullock, the council's director of highways, said.

"Flags, banners and bunting attached to lamp-posts, road signs, roundabouts or other highway infrastructure without permission can create safety risks for road users and pedestrians and may obstruct visibility."

The local authority said it has "a responsibility to keep the highway safe, clear and accessible for everyone".

Bath and North East Somerset Council said it has no plan to introduce measures against hanging unauthorised flags.

articles.standfirst: Bordalás le da a los suyos varios días de descanso para volver con las pilas cargadas tras el parón
articles.summary: Bordalás le da a los suyos varios días de descanso para volver con las pilas cargadas tras el parón
articles.body: “Esto es un sinvivir”, decía José Bordalás tras el encuentro frente al Málaga de esta pasada jornada. Los azulones, que lograron el segundo triunfo del curso, se marchan al parón de selecciones con ocho puntos y el equipo en mitad de tabla. Y veinte días para volver a competir. Y es que ese sinvivir Bordalás quiere transformarlo en una carga de pilas completa porque lo que se le viene al equipo ya lo ha catalogado el alicantino como el “Tourmalet” de los azulones. Por ello, el alicantino le ha dado a los suyos varios días de descanso para que ese cansancio que el entrenador acusó de su vestuario sea subsanado. Bordalás señaló que estas últimas jornadas el equipo ha sufrido una gran fatiga al jugar prácticamente los mismos jugadores, ya no solo en las siete primeras jornadas ligueras, sino en la previa de Conference League, viaje a Serbia incluido en apenas, todo ello, mes y medio de competición. Es por ello que, a veinte días de que vuelva el Getafe a competir, en el Camp Nou, Bordalás le dará un merecido descanso a su equipo. Después, tras el duelo en el Spotify Camp Nou, los azulones viajarán a Rumanía para debutar, por cuarta vez en su historia, en competición europea. Todo ello con tres semanas seguidas jugando jueves y fin de semana, por lo que el equipo deberá descansar cuerpo y mente para afrontar lo que llegará.
